## What this document does

Participants in the two prequestion conditions answered five prequestions on their topic
before reading (Polio or TB). This document describes how much they knew and compares the
two conditions. Each prequestion is scored as the points earned out of its maximum (1–4
points) and modelled with a **beta-binomial** model (points out of the question's
maximum, with overdispersion), with random intercepts for participants and questions.
Condition varies between participants and between questions (each condition answered its
own five questions), so no random slopes are possible.

The comparison TB − Polio is summarized by the posterior mean, 95% credible interval and
probability of direction (pd) on the response scale (the proportion of a question's
points), averaged over the sample. It is **described, not tested**: each condition answered
its own five questions, so condition is confounded with the set of questions, and no
comparison can separate prior knowledge from question difficulty. (A Savage–Dickey Bayes
factor would depend on how the question random effects enter the comparison: the
response-scale contrast, the link-scale contrast averaged over the sample, and the
population-level coefficient disagree.) Shared code (priors,
fitting, Bayes factors) is in `R/bayes_helpers.R`; the fit is cached in
`analysis/brms_cache/`.

## Setup

```{r}
#| label: setup
library(here)
fit_settings <- list(chains = 4, iter = 11000, warmup = 1000, adapt_delta = 0.95, refit = FALSE)
if (exists("params")) {
  fit_settings <- modifyList(fit_settings, params[intersect(names(params), names(fit_settings))])
}
source(here("R", "setup.R"))
source(here("R", "data.R"))
source(here("R", "bayes_helpers.R"))
```

## Descriptives

```{r}
#| label: descriptives
# Participant-level scores (grade_prequestions.R), analysed participants
preq_perf <- read_csv(here("data", "derived", "preq_scored_participants.csv"), show_col_types = FALSE) |>
  filter(et_id %in% levels(dat$participant)) |>
  transmute(participant = et_id, condition = recode(et_group, Po = "Polio"),
            pre = points / max_points, attempted = n_answered / n_questions)
preq_perf |>
  group_by(condition) |>
  summarise(n = n(), mean_score = mean(pre), sd_score = sd(pre), attempted = mean(attempted)) |>
  kable(digits = 3, caption = "Prequestion scores (proportion of the points) and proportion of prequestions attempted")
```

## Model

```{r}
#| label: fit
#| results: hide
preq_items <- read_csv(here("data", "derived", "preq_scored_items.csv"), show_col_types = FALSE) |>
  filter(et_id %in% levels(dat$participant)) |>
  transmute(participant = factor(et_id),
            condition = factor(recode(et_group, Po = "Polio"), levels = c("TB", "Polio")),
            question = factor(questnum), points, max_points)
contrasts(preq_items$condition) <- contr.equalprior_pairs

m_preq <- fit_betabin("condition", "bayes_preq_betabin", preq_items,
                      re = "(1 | participant) + (1 | question)", cor = FALSE)
```

```{r}
#| label: diagnostics
diag_tab <- diag_model(m_preq, "prequestions")
diag_tab
```

```{r}
#| label: fig-ppc
#| fig-width: 7
#| fig-height: 4
ppc_scores(m_preq, "Prequestions: observed and predicted scores")
```

## TB − Polio

```{r}
#| label: comparison
preq_means <- resp_means(m_preq, "condition", predict = "mu")
preq_diff <- estimate_contrasts(m_preq, contrast = "condition", comparison = "revpairwise",
                                predict = "mu", backend = "marginaleffects",
                                estimate = "average", centrality = "mean") |>
  as.data.frame()
preq_means
preq_diff
```

## Prior sensitivity

```{r}
#| label: priorsense
sens_tab <- sens_table(list(prequestions = m_preq))
sens_tab
```

## Results file

```{r}
#| label: save-results
save_results(list(preq_means = preq_means, preq_diff = preq_diff,
                  diag = diag_tab, sens = sens_tab),
             here("analysis", "results_prequestions.rds"))
```
